title: Protozoan loricas form by adsorption into least-area surfaces, not for protection

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Protozoan loricas form by adsorption into least-area surfaces, not for protection

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The membranous cups (loricas) of Salpingoeca, Tintinnus and similar protozoa arise inevitably from substances adsorbed in the surface layer of the protoplasm, and molecular forces make the resulting pellicle a surface of least possible area under the circumstances, here an unduloid; this efficient cause, rather than a protective purpose, explains their form.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. V: The Forms of Cells

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: that this surface pellicle or membrane was inevitably bound, by molecular forces, to become a surface of the least possible area which the circumstances permitted

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter V, “The Forms of Cells”; topic “Physical versus teleological explanation”. Scope: loricate protozoa such as Salpingoeca, Tintinnus, Dinobryon and Codonella

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch05-18: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.44

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The geometric and adsorption mechanism has measurable consequences, but endpoint images cannot establish inevitability or causal assembly. Existing data are especially weak for separating physical formation from a protective evolutionary function.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Image lorica formation in living protozoa while measuring material adsorption and boundary geometry, then test whether the developing pellicle minimizes area under measured constraints and whether blocking adsorption prevents formation. Protection would be assessed separately through survival experiments and cannot be excluded by geometric fit alone.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Minimum-area fit does not distinguish efficient cause from adaptive function.

Lorica materials and boundary conditions vary among taxa.

Formation movies and adsorption measurements for the named taxa are scarce.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The least-area geometry can be tested the same way as other unduloid claims, but only by compiling images, and only for a few loricate genera. The denial of a protective purpose does not change any predicted measurement: a well-fitting unduloid can still be protective. Adsorption as the route by which the pellicle forms is likewise missing from the morphological record, so existing data reach only the shape proxy.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Fit loricas of Salpingoeca, Tintinnus and similar protozoa to the least-area surface available given their attachments, typically an unduloid, and ask whether form is fixed by that fit. A least-area match would support the geometric half. A protective purpose is not a separate measurable outcome, so it cannot be scored against the efficient-cause wording.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lorica outlines are scattered in taxonomic plates.

Protection is not an observable rival to set against a surface fit.

Adsorption into the surface film, as against secreted wall material, is not recorded with the outline.
